title: Affine eigensection charts for a supplied linearized ample line
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $T=\mathbf G_{m,S}$ [def-sfb-relative-split-torus]. Let $X\to S$ be a separated finite-type scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose $a:T\times_SX\to X$ is an action satisfying the unit and associativity identities as scheme maps [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], with a supplied $T$-linearization: an isomorphism $\theta:p_2^*L\simeq a^*L$ [def-pc-module-pullback] restricting to the identity at $1\in T$ and satisfying $\theta_{gh,x}=\theta_{g,hx}\theta_{h,x}$ on $T\times_ST\times_SX$. For every point $x\in X$ there are integers $n\geq1$, $w\in\mathbf Z$ and a section $s\in\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$ such that $x\in X_s$, the nonvanishing open $X_s$ is affine and $T$-invariant, and $s$ is an eigensection of weight $w$ for the induced tensor-power linearization. Explicitly, for every $A$-algebra $B$ and $t\in B^\times$, the action on sections $(t\cdot s_B)(y)=\theta^{\otimes n}_{t,t^{-1}y}(s_B(t^{-1}y))$ equals $t^w s_B$ as a section on $X_B$, including for nonreduced and nonflat $B$. No assertion that invariant affine opens form a basis for arbitrary opens, or that global sections commute with nonflat base change, is made.

source.place: Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample, ideal-section argument, combined with the existing relative split-torus invariant-affine theorem and the normalized Laurent section coaction. This polarized eigensection refinement is an agent-formulated auxiliary, not the verbatim statement of 01Q3. Weight decomposition and flat Laurent base change were also read in groupoids.tex and coherent.tex.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty there is no point to consider. Fix $x\in X$. The single affine open $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a Noetherian affine cover, so $S$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. It is quasi-compact, hence is a Noetherian scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-split-torus-invariant-affines] with rank one, the given normal separated finite-type $X/S$, and the ample line $L$. Obtain an invariant affine open $U$ containing $x$. Invariance also holds for inverse group elements: for every field extension and group element, a point belongs to $U$ if and only if its translate does, by applying invariance once to that element and once to its inverse.

source.place: Agent assembly using the existing relative invariant-affine theorem; Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample, ideal-section argument starts with an affine neighbourhood.

proof.text: Put $Z=|X|\setminus|U|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], its vanishing ideal $\mathcal I_Z$ is quasi-coherent, has zero set $Z$, and consists on each open of regular functions vanishing in the residue fields of all its points in $Z$. The ample definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] gives quasi-compactness of $X$. Since $x\notin Z$, [lem-sc-ample-ideal-section] supplies $n>0$ and $u\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal I_Z\otimes L^{\otimes n})$ whose image in $\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$ is nonzero at $x$. Denote that image by $u$ too. In a local frame its coefficient lies in $\mathcal I_Z$, so its value at every $z\in Z$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample, (1) implies (6) and the proof of (6) implies (1); schemes.tex Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme.

proof.text:
Tensoring the supplied linearization $n$ times gives a linearization on $M=L^{\otimes n}$: the unit and cocycle identities tensor to the same identities. The local rank-one tensor frames show that $M$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-linearized-line-sections-coaction] to $M$ with $C=A[t,t^{-1}]$. Write its finite Laurent expansion as $c(u)=\sum_w u_w\otimes t^w$, with $u_w\in\Gamma(X,M)$ and zero coefficients outside a finite set. The counit identity gives $u=\sum_wu_w$. Coassociativity gives
$$\sum_w c(u_w)\otimes t^w=\sum_wu_w\otimes t^w\otimes t^w.$$
Taking the coefficient of $t^w$ in the last Laurent factor yields $c(u_w)=u_w\otimes t^w$. Coefficient extraction is valid for any $A$-module because $A[t,t^{-1}]=\bigoplus_{w\in\mathbf Z}At^w$; it uses neither a field nor finite generation of the section module.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, as packaged in the cited normalized section coaction; elementary comparison of Laurent coefficients in its coassociativity and counit identities.

proof.text:
Every $u_w$ still vanishes at every point of $Z$. To check this without a base-change isomorphism for $Z$, fix $z\in Z$, put $K=\kappa(z)$ and $B=K(v)$, the rational function field in an indeterminate $v$. Regard $v$ as a point of $T(B)=B^\times$, and let $z_B:\operatorname{Spec}B\to X_B$ be the constant lift of $z$. By Step 1, the point $v^{-1}z_B$ is outside $U_B$, so its image in $X$ lies in $Z$. Hence the section $u_B$ evaluates to zero there, by the residue-field vanishing description in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The normalized all-algebras formula in [lem-sfb-relative-linearized-line-sections-coaction], evaluated at $z_B$, now gives
$$0=(v\cdot u_B)(z_B)=\sum_w v^w u_w(z)\quad\text{in }M(z)\otimes_K K(v),$$
where $M(z)=M_z\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,z}}K$ is a one-dimensional $K$-space. Choose a basis of this line. The displayed equality is a finite Laurent polynomial over $K$ which is zero in $K(v)$. Multiplication by a sufficiently high power of $v$ makes it a polynomial, whose coefficients must all be zero because $v$ is indeterminate. Thus $u_w(z)=0$ for all $w$. This tests the boundary over a field only; it asserts no commutation of global sections with any nonflat base change.

source.place: Agent Laurent-coefficient argument preserving the boundary vanishing used in Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample; normalized coaction from coherent.tex Tag 02KH.

proof.text: Since $u(x)=\sum_wu_w(x)\ne0$, some coefficient $s=u_w$ has $s(x)\ne0$. Step 4 implies $X_s\subseteq U$. Apply [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] to the global section $s$ of $L^{\otimes n}$ and the affine open $U$: it states that $U\cap X_s$ is affine, and this intersection is exactly $X_s$. Thus $x\in X_s$ and $X_s$ is affine. The value and nonvanishing criteria here are those of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 01PV, lemma-affine-cap-s-open; final affine-neighbourhood argument in Tag 01Q3, proposition-characterize-ample.

proof.text: Step 3 gives $c(s)=s\otimes t^w$. The final clause of [lem-sfb-relative-linearized-line-sections-coaction] therefore gives $t\cdot s_B=t^ws_B$ as an equality of sections for every $A$-algebra $B$ and every $t\in B^\times$, with exactly the action formula in the statement. This also proves scheme-theoretic invariance of $X_s$. Apply the formula with the universal group element on $T\times_S X_s$: the relation says $\theta^{\otimes n}_{t,y}(s(y))=t^w s(ty)$. The left side is a generator of the pulled-back line, and $t^w$ is a unit, so $s(ty)$ is a generator. The action consequently lands in the open subscheme $X_s$ and restricts there; the identity and associativity laws restrict from $X$. This generator criterion works over arbitrary rings, including nonreduced and nonflat $B$.

source.place: Tag 02KH through the cited coaction normalization; unit-generator criterion for the nonvanishing locus, Properties Definition 01PS.
